author: visegrad24
text:
🇧🇾🇵🇱 Lukashenko’s regime in Belarus is marking the day of the 1939 Soviet invasion of Poland with anti-Polish propaganda.

Minsk sells the story that Poland is about to attack or annex western Belarus, and it has built a new state holiday, National Unity Day, on the anniversary of that invasion.

The talking points are copied from the old Soviet playbook. Lukashenko presents that period as an occupation and “ethnocide of the Belarusian people.”

Western Belarus did develop more slowly than central Poland and suffered unemployment. But people there had private property, land, free trade and freedom of worship.

Soviet Eastern Belarus at that time had collectivization, gulags, the Great Terror, famine and the mass-murder of the Belarusian national elite. 

The mass murder site of Kurapaty and the Night of the Executed Poets were part of that system. 

Kurapaty was the primary execution site used by the Minsk NKVD between 1937 and 1941. Historians estimate that up to 250 000 victims of Stalinist terror were buried there.

Belarusians living the Polish Second Republic did not face Stalin’s shooting grounds.

Regime propaganda claims western Belarusians met the Red Army in 1939 with flowers and tears of joy at the fall of Polish rule. That euphoria, where it existed, lasted weeks. The NKVD followed right behind the Red Army. 

Mass deportations to Siberia and Kazakhstan, arrests, shuttered private shops, forced collectivization of farms followed. 

Well-off peasants, the intelligentsia, and even Belarusian socialists soon saw what “Soviet liberation” meant.

The Bereza Kartuska concentration camp in Poland is heavily emphasized in Lukashenko's new propaganda anti-Polish campaign. Minsk says it was a camp created to oppress Belarusians.

In reality, the first inmates to arrive at Bereza Kartuska were Polish nationalists. 

Then came members of the Communist Party of Poland and the underground Communist Parties of Western Belarus and Western Ukraine which made up a majority of the prisoners.

Later, they were joined by members of the Organization of Ukrainian Nationalists (OUN), Belarusian nationalists, smugglers, common criminals and Nazi spies. It was a site holding mainly political prisoners under harsh conditions but not a site of mass murder. Around a dozen people of people died there over the course of 5 years while more than 3,000 inmates passed through the facility.

Lukashenko's new anti-Polish campaign serves his regime at home. 

Lukashenko invents an “inevitable attempt of new Polish occupation” of western Belarus to manufacture an external enemy, distract from the country's economic crisis, justify his repression of Belarusian civil society and the Polish minority while also blaming his diplomatic and economic mess on “Western plots.” 

Lukashenko is also eager to align with Russian state propaganda, which has also intensified its efforts to demonize Poland since the Kremlin launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
